match.reason: None of the bank points teaches adding or multiplying functions or sketching their graphs by combining heights; they cover limiting sums, power functions, domain and range, relations, and modelling, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Sums and products of functions
card: (f + g)(x) = f(x) + g(x) and (f × g)(x) = f(x) × g(x). Each is built by working with the two outputs at the same x value.
The new function exists only where both f and g exist. Its domain is the overlap of the two domains.
To sketch f + g, add the heights of the two graphs at each x. To sketch f × g, multiply the heights. Where one height is 0, the product is 0.
Example: f(x) = x² with domain R, and g(x) = √x with domain [0, ∞). Then (f + g)(4) = 16 + 2 = 18, and the domain of f + g is [0, ∞).
draft.remember: Combine the outputs at the same x, and only use x values that both functions allow.

a.q: f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x². What is (f × g)(3)?
a.why: f(3) = 7 and g(3) = 9, so the product is 7 × 9 = 63. The answer 16 comes from adding the outputs, which gives f + g, not f × g.
a.clue: Find each output at x = 3, then multiply them.

b.q: f(x) = √(x − 2) and g(x) = 1/(x − 5). What is the domain of f + g?
b.why: f needs x ≥ 2, and g needs x ≠ 5. The shared domain keeps x ≥ 2 and removes 5. R except x = 5 ignores the limit from f.
b.clue: Check what each function rules out, then keep only what both allow.

final.title: Sums and products of functions
card: \((f + g)(x) = f(x) + g(x)\) and \((f \times g)(x) = f(x) \times g(x)\). Each is built by working with the two outputs at the same \(x\) value.
The new function exists only where both \(f\) and \(g\) exist. Its domain is the overlap of the two domains.
To sketch \(f + g\), add the heights of the two graphs at each \(x\). To sketch \(f \times g\), multiply the heights. Where one height is 0, the product is 0.
Example: \(f(x) = x^{2}\) with domain \(\mathbb{R}\), and \(g(x) = \sqrt{x}\) with domain \([0, \infty)\). Then \((f + g)(4) = 16 + 2 = 18\), and the domain of \(f + g\) is \([0, \infty)\).
final.remember: Combine the outputs at the same \(x\), and only use \(x\) values that both functions allow.
